scientometricsInR 0.2.0

Maintenance review — 30 October–2 November 2026

Purpose and acceptance criteria

A scientometrics teaching book and companion R package for researchers, librarians and research administrators. This local milestone requires truthful analytical labels, preserved author/data provenance, explicit provider failures, a usable reading site, inspectable publication files and an installable companion archive. Hosted CI, publication and scientific/editorial acceptance are separate gates.

The roadmap prioritised (1) incorrect results and claims, (2) dependable provider and package behaviour, (3) executable onboarding and readable publication formats. A frozen, licensed corpus and a fully pinned toolchain remain a later milestone; adding more methods was outside this repair pass.

Confirmed findings and completed repairs

  • High — incorrect scientific labels. Chapters 10/11/13 and related solutions called within-sample ratios or cumulative citations world-normalized MNCS, JIF/SNIP, or institutional productivity. They now state the actual samples, denominators and reference construction; undefined values remain missing. Chapter 14’s related exercise distinguishes publication cohorts from citation receipt windows. Chapters 31/32/33 now distinguish ordinary scholarly citations, descriptive cohort interactions and access metadata from patent evidence, causal effects and reproducibility measures. These distinctions prevent readers from treating available metadata as evidence for an unmeasured outcome.
  • High — wrong entities. Chapter 13 and Case Study 2 included invalid institution IDs and a University of Zurich ID labelled ETH Zurich. Chapter 11 included three invalid journal IDs and Current Forestry Reports labelled Quantitative Science Studies. Current identities were checked against OpenAlex records, corrected, and exercised. Empty/failed comparisons stop instead of silently losing entities.
  • High — unsupported demographic inference. Chapter 28 and Case Study 4 assigned genders to real authors using short unvalidated name lists. Their mechanics are now illustrated with explicitly synthetic records and arbitrary categories, retaining unmatched records and making no empirical gender-gap claim.
  • High — mislabeled keyword method. The previous milestone replaced unigram frequency ranking with basic RAKE (R/rake_keywords.R), including a hand-computed regression, and removed unsupported universal accuracy percentages. Extraction quality still needs evaluation on a defined annotated corpus.
  • High — identity and missingness. R/utils.R preserves stable author IDs in graph vertex name, with human-readable label/display_name; homonyms stay separate and repeated work/author records do not inflate edges. Institutional fractional credit requires usable affiliations for every listed author. R/funding_helpers.R rejects missing funder IDs rather than counting NA as funding. Chapters 17/CS03 distinguish OpenAlex topics from their parent taxonomy levels.
  • Medium — provider reliability and preservation. R/api_helpers.R uses exact argument caches, atomic replacement and explicit offline hit/miss behaviour. Exhausted HTTP warnings from openalexR now fail rather than becoming apparent empty successes. Tracked teaching fixtures are unchanged and documented as synthetic. Generated live exports go to _freeze/exports.
  • Medium — execution and distribution. Added a shared 53-package installer for readers and CI, including the missing reshape2 dependency. Historical renv and Docker paths are explicitly unqualified; Appendix A now describes bookdown/docs. PDF text and Cairo figures select a Unicode-capable font to preserve non-Latin author labels; tables and code wrap within the page. PDF printing settings are restored before subsequent HTML/EPUB renders in the same R session. The method navigator is readable, keyboard-scrollable and unnumbered; chapter numbering is consistent. Available-file inventories replace unconditional download links. Optional chapter PDF generation reports failure through its exit status. The download list is also available in mobile navigation; it no longer depends on a desktop-only sidebar.
  • Medium — EPUB packaging. The rendered EPUB contained malformed XHTML, missing citation/licence files and cross-chapter links that pointed into the wrong chapter. The explicit packaging step repairs only deterministic targets, bundles the source assets and validates the result before replacing the input. Ambiguous or missing targets fail without replacing the original ebook. CI and first-use instructions include this step before publishing a download inventory.
  • Medium — validation before publication. Manual book and package CI runs previously also deployed their output. Manual runs now default to build-only; publication requires selecting the explicit deploy input. Manual book runs retain a downloadable review artifact. Existing main-push and scheduled deployment behaviour is unchanged. Hosted execution remains unverified.
  • Packaging. Preserve the separate prose/code licences and original authorship. Exclude caches, live exports, figures, temporary HTML and TeX logs from the companion source archive, including when a book render is in progress.

Observed verification

All seven R files pass lintr with zero findings and styler without changes. The style repairs preserve parsed expressions apart from two explicit internal-helper renames and single-statement braces; neither check was relaxed. The final HTML, PDF and EPUB were rebuilt on 31 October from source commit b050100 in separate worktrees and fresh R processes. Every analysis chunk was re-executed with copies of the verified provider caches. All three builds succeeded, and every tracked source file still matched its committed Git blob. Final artifact review and local distribution assembly completed on 2 November. The subsequent HTML-only mobile download fix was synchronized from style/after-body.html into all 59 reading pages. Reversing that exact fragment restores every pre-update byte; analysis, search content, PDF and EPUB were unchanged. The preserved full-build outputs and fragment hashes document this final UI update separately.

R 4.6.1 on macOS arm64. Authentication and a cursor request returned HTTP 200; no credential was placed in source. An initial render stopped at Chapter 22 on missing reshape2; this was installed in the audit library and added to the shared dependency inventory. Earlier failures are retained in the audit logs.

  • The final companion source archive passed R CMD check --no-manual --no-vignettes, Status OK, with 126 passing assertions, no warnings or skips. It contains 43 members (29,468 bytes), and every source-backed member matches this checkout. No generated or live-data files are included. A separate build during active PDF compilation also excluded all TeX auxiliary files. The checked archive SHA256 is bee3e3b308e148bb48732272eaa7194a55daa0d9a4dbbd72b844769c8017e33f.
  • Fresh installation and first use of that final archive passed: bundled datasets, independently calculated RAKE scores and offline cache hit/miss behaviour.
  • All 53 required package namespaces load. All 67 configured Rmd files parse. Independent checks cover author identity, partial affiliations, missing funding, normalization, synthetic categories, descriptive interactions, actual cached institution/journal/topic workflows and repaired solution snippets.
  • Download inventory and browser visibility cases pass. Desktop/mobile search, navigation, corrected content and the readable method diagram were observed. Final desktop and mobile download responses match the qualified file hashes; mobile EPUB click/save and PDF navigation passed. Missing inventories show no download links, and there are no duplicate download IDs or advertised missing chapter PDFs. The final site has 59 HTML pages and 8,013 checked local references, with no broken targets or visible unresolved references. Search contains 866 sections across 58 content pages. scripts/verify-render-formats.R also passes PDF, repeated-PDF, HTML and EPUB transitions without leaking table/device settings.
  • EPUB packaging passes 35 regression checks and a byte-identical repeat run. The final ebook has 161 archive members, 65 XHTML documents and 8,620 checked internal references. Official EPUBCheck 5.4.0 with --failonwarnings reports zero findings. Independent comparison preserves all 92 other original assets byte-for-byte and all 62 original XHTML text sequences without substitutions. Representative tables and citation/licence fallback pages were visually checked, including a 390-pixel viewport. These are XHTML rendering checks, not acceptance in every dedicated ebook reader.
  • The PDF typography specimens and 11 format regression groups pass, including exact DOI/header/code content, repeated spaces, Unicode names, grouped tables, hidden columns and plain-output wrapping. The final 609-page PDF has no missing glyphs, undefined references, replacement characters or extracted words outside the page. Eleven representative final pages were independently viewed, including repaired tables, qualified scientific claims, Unicode labels and the b050100 colophon. This is representative inspection, not page-by-page proofing.
  • Manual publication controls passed YAML parsing and deployment/artifact event checks. Manual workflows default to validation without publication; hosted execution remains unobserved.

First use and release boundary

Follow README’s installer and render commands from this candidate checkout. Serve existing output with python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory docs and visit http://localhost:8000. Configure an activated OpenAlex key outside Git for uncached requests. SCIENTOMETRICS_REBUILD_CHUNKS=1 re-executes analysis while retaining exact-query provider caches. SCIENTOMETRICS_OFFLINE=1 covers OpenAlex only and cannot replace missing caches. Graph display names are in label or display_name; name now intentionally holds stable author IDs.

The full book’s historical lockfile/Docker restore, installation of all book packages into an otherwise empty machine, optional Python/SQL/OCR backends and live Shiny/deployment exercises remain unqualified. Exercise-solution chunks are intentionally unevaluated by the book renderer; repaired snippets were checked independently, but not every solution was executed. Minor upstream deprecation messages, front-matter subsection numbering and repeated callout headings are deferred. The PDF retains 152 minor overfull-box warnings (contents, running heads and body/table margins; maximum 29.03 pt); representative affected content remains readable. This pass does not constitute independent scientific or editorial acceptance of the entire text.

Next release action: review the candidate and rendered books. After authorization, push the review branch, configure the GitHub OPENALEX_API_KEY secret, and run the manual book/package workflows on that revision with deploy unchecked. Review their results and the book artifact before an authorized publication. The existing main-push and scheduled workflows still deploy automatically, so a push to main is a publication step. No push, merge, deployment or submission occurred.
